analysis.title: Market Update US, Europe & Asia, 18 November 2026
key_insights: US equities fell for a second day on Tuesday: S&P 500 -1.03%, Dow -1.64%, Nasdaq -0.74%, Russell 2000 -1.49%. Decliners outnumbered gainers by nearly 6:1, the third-worst breadth reading year to date, and all sectors closed lower.
The S&P 500 closed below its 200-day moving average for the first time since early April. The 10-day cumulative advance/decline line is below -400, down from +921 at the 21-Oct peak.

The AI trade did not bounce. Semiconductors, memory and neoclouds were largely lower and Nvidia fell again, with tighter export controls and AI buildout funding concerns cited. Treasury yields fell 2-4 bp.

Factor rotation was sharp over five days: low volatility (SPLV) beat high beta (SPHB) by over 460 bp and quality (QUAL) beat it by 280 bp. BofA says AI groups still rank top on its Triple Momentum screen, which it reads as intact earnings momentum. Mizuho calls the selloff an indiscriminate buyers strike driven by systematic degrossing.

October retail sales rose 0.2% m/m, in line with consensus, after +0.8% in September (revised higher). Ex-autos rose 0.6% vs +0.4% consensus and control-group sales rose 0.6% vs +0.3% consensus. Industrial production unexpectedly fell, import and export prices were notably higher than expected, and NAHB homebuilder sentiment hit a 14-year low.

Fed speakers were hawkish. Musalem (non-voter) argued for several hikes and a 2-2.5% real policy rate by spring. Williams said conditions do not warrant aggressive action. The October FOMC minutes are due Wednesday 18-Nov at 14:00 ET, after a hold at 3.75%-4.00% with two dissents for a 25 bp hike.

BofA and Goldman Sachs have each added a third 25 bp hike to their forecasts (Goldman in Mar-27). BofA expects the minutes to show a deeper committee divide than the two dissents. Waller has raised the possibility of a 50 bp December hike if inflation runs hot.

Nvidia reports Q3 after the close on 17-Nov and the Street expects a beat and raise. Focus is on FY28 guidance of about 70% revenue growth, export restrictions and AI buildout funding. Huang said he would return as CEO if requested, but the board says a return is not under consideration. It formed a committee on national security and export controls.

A Commerce Department interim rule would require non-US data center operators in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil to get a US license before exporting advanced US AI chips to customers there. China said it would take 'necessary measures'. Z.AI and MiniMax are down more than 25% month to date, while SMIC, Hua Hong and Cambricon are outperforming.

European equities fell sharply: DAX -2.08%, FTSE 100 -1.76%, CAC -1.62%. Tech, miners, luxury and autos led declines, while energy and travel and leisure held up best. Tech extended its sell-off on AI return and valuation concerns, and copper fell on weak China growth data.

German ZEW for November was 35.6 vs 29.0 expected and 28.1 prior, the highest since February. UK unemployment was 4.6% but payrolled employees fell 34K in October and regular pay growth slowed to 3.5%. The data is unlikely to deter a December BoE hike, although most economists expect a hold.
Spain's de Cos is the front-runner to succeed Lagarde as ECB president after Knot withdrew. A formal decision is expected at the 26-27 November EU summit.

Le Pen's pension plan would return the legal retirement age to 60-62 and add a mandatory capitalisation pillar. The OAT-Bund spread narrowed 3 bp to 152 bp. Goldman Sachs sees Le Pen as the clear favourite but a parliamentary majority as uncertain, and expects French bonds to underperform EU peers through mid-2027.
Asian equities fell: Nikkei -1.34%, Hang Seng -1.03%, Shanghai -0.50%. Korea, Taiwan and Australia fell steeply, while India rose 0.38%.

RBA minutes show the board debated a hold vs a hike in November, and Bullock says inflation risks are skewed to the upside. Economists called China's October activity data bearish: fixed asset investment lagged and retail was weak. 2026 growth is seen just reaching the 4.5-5.0% target range, with 2027 at 4.0-4.5%.
Trump meets Xi at APEC in Shenzhen this week. Little concrete progress is expected, and the US-China trade truce runs through 10-Jan.

Large US single-stock moves: Nike -6.3% (FY28 guided lower despite better FY31 targets), UnitedHealth -5.4% (CMS proposed CRUSH fraud rule), Home Depot -2.5% (Q3 comps +2.2%, 50 bp above consensus; gross margin missed by 20 bp), Bill Holdings +12.6% (TPG reportedly nearing a take-private), Energizer +12.6% (FQ4 beat), AECOM +11.1% (FQ4 modest beat).

market_movers.rationale: Goldman Sachs upgraded from neutral to buy, citing EBITDA growth potential from natural and organic products, better execution and network optimization. Shares rose 7.4%.
Bernstein cut to underperform from market perform, expecting an EPS miss next year on North America pressure. Shares fell 3%.
Morgan Stanley cut Moncler to underweight on heavy Asia exposure (about 66% of sales), declining like-for-like volumes and margin pressure, with 2027/28 EPS well below consensus.
Oddo cut Stellantis to underperform, expecting raw-material and electronic-component inflation to limit savings and leave the 2027 AOI margin at 1.6% and industrial free cash flow at -€2.2B.
Oddo cut JCDecaux to neutral. It is confident in 6.1% organic growth in 2026 but sees limited upside after the re-rating to 16x 2027 earnings.
Barclays cut Swiss Life to equal weight on a premium valuation to peers, lower-for-longer Swiss rates and limited near-term EPS catalysts.
Barclays reinstated Zurich Insurance at equal weight. It supports the Beazley deal but sees limited upside as global commercial P&C softens.

Goldman Sachs initiated SBM Offshore at buy as best placed for the deepwater cycle in Guyana, Brazil and West Africa, with a roughly 40% FPSO market share. 2027 award announcements are the key catalyst.
Goodbody initiated Barclays at buy, seeing the greatest re-rating potential on better execution, diversified revenue and capital allocation.
The FT reported TPG is nearing a take-private deal with an agreement expected in coming days. Shares rose 12.6%.
CMS proposed the CRUSH rule to strengthen fraud oversight across Medicare, Medicaid, CHIP and the Marketplace. Shares fell 5.4% and managed-care names broadly lagged.
At its investor day Nike guided FY28 lower and called it a challenging year, while guiding FY31 operating margin and EPS above expectations. Shares fell 6.3%.
Q3 comps beat but the gross margin missed, the implied Q4 guide looked light and the CEO transition adds risk. Shares fell 2.5%.

sector_views.rationale: Energy outperformed in both the US and Europe during the selloff.
Tech led European declines and AI-linked groups were weak in the US on export controls and funding concerns. BofA still sees AI momentum as intact on its screen.
Managed care lagged after the CMS CRUSH fraud rule proposal.

earnings_insights: Nvidia Q3: reports 17-Nov after the close. The Street expects a beat and raise, and the focus is on current FY28 guidance of about 70% revenue growth.

Home Depot Q3 (reported): comps +2.2%, 50 bp better than consensus. Gross margin missed by 20 bp and EPS was slightly ahead. The implied Q4 guide looked light. CFO Richard McPhail becomes CEO on 23-Nov.

Disney FQ4 (reported): EPS, revenue and FCF all beat. Entertainment drove the revenue upside on higher subscription fees. Q1 operating income guided ahead and FY27 EPS growth guidance reaffirmed. Analysts see continued Hong Kong and Shanghai pressure through FY27.
Nike (investor day): FY28 guided lower, FY31 operating margin and EPS guided above expectations.
Energizer FQ4 (reported): earnings and margins beat, revenue largely in line, organic decline narrower than consensus.
AECOM FQ4 (reported): EPS and EBITDA modestly beat and net service revenue was in line. Backlog rose 13% y/y to $28B. FY27 guidance was largely in line with organic revenue growth of 4-6%.
Amer Sports Q3 (reported): beat, FY guidance raised for all three segments, and a $1B buyback announced.
Omeros Q3 (reported): earnings better but revenue missed, R&D above consensus. Shares fell 16.6%.
NIBE Q3 (reported): revenue SEK 11.23B vs SEK 11.08B estimate, operating income SEK 1.52B vs SEK 1.42B consensus, EPS SEK 0.44 vs SEK 0.45 estimate.
Diploma FY26 (reported): EPS growth of 45% on 15% organic revenue growth. FY27 guidance is 12% revenue growth and a 25.5% EBITA margin.
Big Yellow H1 (reported): beat on revenue, store EBITDA and EPS, but EPRA NTA fell 10.1% and post-period occupancy and pricing weakened.
IQE: second FY outlook upgrade, now expecting revenue growth above 40% and adjusted EBITDA in the mid-teens £M.
KE Holdings and XPeng Q3 (reported): headline figures beat estimates. SK Square Q3 operating profit +200% y/y. Dentsu Q3 with FY guidance below estimates.
Retail earnings due this week: Walmart, Target, TJX, Lowe's and Ross Stores.
